memory_candidates.content: jq has no formatting-preserving mode: it parses input to a value and serializes that value back out in jq's own fixed style. Piping an entire JSON file through jq -- even with a filter scoped to a few fields -- reflows every record's layout, including records the filter never touches. For a JSON file with hand-maintained layout (mixed compact/expanded records, deliberate key order) where the edit is meant to touch only a few fields, use a text-level edit against the HEAD bytes instead, then assert equivalence via `diff <(jq -S . text-edited) <(jq -S . jq-computed)` before moving the result into place. The assertion is load-bearing: it buys back jq's well-formedness/intended-value guarantee that a bare text edit gives up.
